parsed.summary: The formal statements prove three things about R_k(3), defined as the least n such that every k-colouring of E(K_n) has a monochromatic triangle. First, R_k(3)^{1/k} → ∞. Second, for every ε>0 and all sufficiently large k, (1/3−ε)k log k ≤ log R_k(3) ≤ (1+ε)k log k. Third, log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k). The most important caveat is that `erdos_problem_183_explicit`, which is meant to capture the explicit bound of Theorem 1.1 for all k ≥ 2, carries the false hypothesis (1:ℕ)=0, so it is vacuous. The non-asymptotic Theorem 1.1 is therefore not actually formalized.

glossary.plain: A k-colouring C of the edges of K_n has no monochromatic triangle: each colour class is K_3-free.
Every k-colouring of E(K_n) contains a monochromatic triangle.
glossary.note: For k=0 and n≥2 no colourings exist, so the statement holds vacuously. This only affects k=0.

glossary.plain: R_k(3) = min{n : every k-colouring of E(K_n) has a monochromatic triangle}, defined via sInf.
glossary.note: The set is nonempty for every k by Ramsey's theorem, so the sInf ∅ = 0 junk value never occurs. The degenerate value R_0 = 2 is irrelevant asymptotically.

lean_claims.plain: R_k(3)^{1/k} → ∞ as k → ∞ (over ℕ, real rpow).
Assuming 1 = 0 in ℕ (false), two things hold: for all k ≥ 2, ((1/(6e^{38}))·k^{1/3}/log k)^k ≤ R_k(3); and R_k(3)^{1/k} → ∞. Because the hypothesis is false, this is vacuous.
For every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large k: (1/3−ε)·k·log k ≤ log R_k(3) ≤ (1+ε)·k·log k.
log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k) as k → ∞.

paper_claims.plain: There is an absolute c > 0 with R_k(3) ≥ (c k^{1/3}/log k)^k for every integer k ≥ 2.

coverage.why: The Lean statement uses an explicit c = 1/(6e^{38}), which would be stronger than the paper. However, the false hypothesis 1 = 0 makes the statement vacuous. The sharp-coefficient theorem is only an eventual, asymptotic consequence of (3), not (3) itself.
Taking logarithms, this is exactly k^{(1/3−o(1))k} ≤ R_k ≤ k^{(1+o(1))k}.
R_k = k^{Θ(k)} is the same as log R_k = Θ(k log k).

flags.explanation: The hypothesis h_mut : (1:ℕ) = 0 is false, so the theorem is vacuously true and certifies nothing. The explicit all-k≥2 lower bound, the paper's headline inequality (3), is therefore not formalized anywhere among the targets.
flags.probe_idea: Restate it without h_mut as ∃ c > 0, ∀ k ≥ 2, (c * k^(1/3) / Real.log k)^k ≤ (triangleRamseyNumber k : ℝ), and check that a proof exists. Alternatively, confirm `example : ¬ ((1:ℕ) = 0) := by decide`.

flags.explanation: The remaining lower bound is only eventual, with exponent (1/3−ε). This is strictly weaker than (c k^{1/3}/log k)^k for all k ≥ 2, which carries the explicit −k log log k + O(k) correction. The asymptotic corollaries are covered, but the quantitative theorem is not.
The edge case k = 0 gives R_0 = 2 because the arrow relation holds vacuously. The sInf set is nonempty for every k, so there is no junk 0 value. This does not affect any of the atTop statements.
